evals.prompt: An agent reported it fixed a null-deref in `src/auth.ts`, anchored by a `// FIX-auth-null` guard comment. I want a tamper-evident check that this fix is still present two sessions from now, after any revert or refactor. How?
evals.expected_output: Run witness.sh sign --namespace=assert-presence <slug>, author a PRESENT_MARKER assertion anchored on the unique fix-id comment (src/auth.ts :: // FIX-auth-null), producing an ed25519-signed manifest at .witness/assert-presence-<slug>.{txt,sig}; verify once locally, commit both files, and wire witness.sh verify --namespace=assert-presence into pre-commit/CI so it exits 2 with ASSERTION REGRESSION if the marker disappears.

assertions.name: uses_sign_script
assertions.description: Response runs scripts/witness.sh sign --namespace=assert-presence <slug> (the bundled ed25519 signer), not a hand-rolled checksum or generic git approach

assertions.name: present_marker_grammar
assertions.description: Response uses a PRESENT_MARKER: <path> :: <substring> assertion anchored on the unique fix-id comment (// FIX-auth-null), not PRESENT_FILE alone

assertions.name: witness_manifest_path_and_sig
assertions.description: Response stores the manifest at .witness/assert-presence-<slug>.txt with an ed25519 .sig and commits both — not .scratch/ or an arbitrary path

assertions.name: verify_gate_wired
assertions.description: Response wires witness.sh verify --namespace=assert-presence into pre-commit/CI and notes it exits 2 / prints ASSERTION REGRESSION when the asserted marker is missing

evals.prompt: To pin that an agent's fix is still there, should I just sha256 the whole file so any change to it trips the check?
evals.expected_output: No — a full-file sha256 is brittle: an unrelated refactor (renaming a variable) breaks the assertion even though the fix is intact. Use a PRESENT_MARKER substring anchored on a unique fix-id comment instead; it survives refactors and only trips when the actual fix is gone.

assertions.name: rejects_whole_file_hash
assertions.description: Response rejects full-file sha256 as brittle — an unrelated refactor would break it — and does NOT endorse hashing the whole file

assertions.name: recommends_present_marker
assertions.description: Response recommends a PRESENT_MARKER substring anchored on a unique fix-id comment as the resilient alternative (skill-documented anti-pattern)
